title: Versioning (Conventional Commits → semver)
html:
English |

Versioning (Conventional Commits → semver)

The version of the kit is decided by the merge, not by a person: every merge to main runs the version workflow, which reads the commit subjects since the last v* tag, classifies them by Conventional Commits and computes the next semver. The tag is the single source of truth - the published npm version always equals the tag. On every bump, the version workflow also commits the version into the repo (chore(release): vX.Y.Z, stamped into all 6 package.json files) and pushes it to main before tagging — the tag is cut on that bump commit, so git show vX.Y.Z:package.json always equals vX.Y.Z and a checkout of the tag is publishable as-is. Direct push by the workflow uses a deploy key (the builtin GITHUB_TOKEN cannot receive ruleset bypass); the publish-time stamp in the release workflow remains as a verification guard. Tags cut before this mechanism (v1.7.2 and earlier) carry the old 1.0.0 placeholder in their tree.

The commit format

<type>(<optional scope>)!: <subject>

optional body
BREAKING CHANGE: <optional footer>

Valid types: feat fix docs style refactor perf test build ci chore revert. Every PR commit (except merge commits) and the PR title are validated by CI — a commit outside the pattern does not enter main, because it would be invisible to the version calculation.

The bump rule

Commits since the last v* tag Bump Example
feat: minor feat(lint): L15 binary manifest check
fix: patch fix(launcher): resolve fallback exit code
any type with !, or BREAKING CHANGE: footer major feat!!: rename init flags
only docs: chore: refactor: test: ci: style: build: none no tag, no release

Precedence is semver's: major > minor > patch. One feat! among ten fix commits bumps the major.

The pipeline

  1. PR (.github/workflows/ci.yml) — three gates in parallel: the test matrix (gofmt, vet, test, build, kit lint ×3 OS), conventional-commits (subjects + PR title) and release-readiness (version sync across the 6 package.json files, npm pack --dry-run shape ×6, cross-compile smoke of the 5 release targets, launcher contract + dispatch + fallback).
  2. Merge to main (.github/workflows/version.yml) — commits since the last tag are classified; no releasable commit ends here silently. With a bump: the annotated vX.Y.Z tag is created on HEAD, pushed, and the release workflow is dispatched explicitly (a tag push made with the GITHUB_TOKEN does not trigger workflows — workflow_dispatch is the documented exception).
  3. Tag (.github/workflows/release.yml) — cross-compiles the 5 platforms with the version stamped by the tag, SHA-256 checksums, GitHub Release (idempotent: create falls back to upload --clobber on re-run), release notes as a Conventional Commits digest, then npm: token pre-flight (npm whoami, fail fast), the 5 platform packages first, the main package last, already-published packages are skipped. Any failed publish turns the job red — the GitHub Release and its assets stay up, and a re-run completes only what is missing.

Tag history note: v1.0.0

The first tag predates this pipeline. v1.0.0 was pushed by hand as a lightweight tag on 5ffacab, half-way up the release/v1.0.0 branch, so the commits that landed after it on that branch — including the feat(ci) that introduced this very version workflow — fell outside the tag and shipped as v1.1.0. That is why the v1.1.0 tag sits on the merge commit of the release/v1.0.0 PR: the merge carried the feat(ci), and feat bumps the minor. The tag stays as-is: it is already published and referenced by npm releases, and re-cutting it would force-push a public tag. Every tag from v1.1.0 on is annotated and created by the workflow.

Manual release

Tags pushed manually (git tag v1.2.3 && git push origin v1.2.3) release through the same path. The release workflow also accepts a manual dispatch (Actions → release → tag), useful to resume an interrupted publish — the npm steps are idempotent.
